newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends near day-high, US rate fears ebb.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends near day-high, US rate fears ebb.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of blue-chip shares ended bourse trade on Monday just off session highs, continuing to draw strength from last Friday's U.S. jobs data that eased worst fears of an imminent U.S. rate increase.
The DAX 30-share index closed 31.73 points, or 1.26 percent, up at 2,548.73, just off a day-high of 2,548.88, on volumes that dealers said were still too limited to launch a stronger move forward.
"Most of the buying that we saw on Friday was short-covering," said one dealer referring to stock purchases designed to cover earlier "sell" positions.
"But people are still a bit sceptical about the future direction," he added. Meanwhile, the stable dollar against the mark and steady bonds were seen providing some support to share prices.

Shares in car-maker Volkswagen closed seven marks higher at 555.25 marks after a weekend German press report that it planned to boost its meagre return on sales ration by tenfold by the end of the decade.
VW chief Ferdinand Piech said he saw U.S.-based Chrysler -- with a return on sales of 6.6 percent compared to VW's 0.6 percent -- as a model for the company.
Commercial bank Deutsche Bank, still suffering image problems after last week's temporary suspension of dealing in three of its British-based funds, traded 39 pfennigs weaker at 71.89 marks.

Airline Deutsche Lufthansa, which started wage talks with its main unions on Monday, ended 5.60 marks up at 206.60 but dealers said the move upwards was more of a correction of recent weakness rather than optimism over the talks, which are seen as likely to be difficult.
